diagnostic_evidence.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed frame scaling system requires ||x_i~||_2 = n/k and sum_i x_i~ x_i~^T = I_n simultaneously. Taking traces of the second condition forces sum_i ||x_i~||^2 = n, but the first condition gives sum_i ||x_i~||^2 = k(n/k)^2 = n^2/k; the system is feasible only if k = n, so as stated it has no solution (e.g., for the experiment's n = 50, k = 55). Moreover the claimed correspondence is wrong: the operator scaling equations give l_i^2 ||R x_i||^2 = 1/k and sum_i l_i^2 (R x_i)(R x_i)^T = (1/n) I_n, so with a_i = n l_i^2 one gets ||x_i~||^2 = n^2 l_i^4 ||R x_i||^2 = (n^2 l_i^2)/k, which is not even constant in i, and sum_i x_i~ x_i~^T = n^2 sum_i l_i^4 (R x_i)(R x_i)^T is not constrained to equal I_n. The consistent equal-norm tight frame target is ||x_i~||_2 = sqrt(n/k); then P = R and a_i = sqrt(n) l_i do satisfy both conditions (||x_i~||^2 = n l_i^2 ||R x_i||^2 = n/k and sum_i x_i~ x_i~^T = n sum_i l_i^2 (R x_i)(R x_i)^T = I_n), and conversely l_i = a_i/sqrt(n) recovers an operator scaling solution, so the intended equivalence holds only after this correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the frame scaling conditions to ||x_i~||_2 = sqrt(n/k) (equivalently ||x_i~||_2^2 = n/k) and the correspondence to P = R, a_i = sqrt(n) l_i. Then both directions of the claimed equivalence follow directly from the two operator scaling equations and the trace identity, and no other part of the paper needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: Only the frame-scaling reduction in the frame scaling experiment subsection is affected: the target problem displayed there is infeasible whenever k != n (in particular for the experiment's n = 50, k = 55), and the stated correspondence a_i = n l_i^2 does not produce a frame scaling solution. No labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, or algorithm depends on the erroneous normalization, and the experiment itself (operator scaling of the CP map Phi(Z) = diag(x_i^T Z x_i) with A_i = e_i x_i^T) is unaffected.
issues.title: Frame scaling conditions are mutually inconsistent and the operator-scaling correspondence is misstated
issues.why_classification: The root defect is a single wrong normalization in one side-claim of the experiments section. The trace identity forces the unique correction sqrt(n/k), which in turn forces a_i = sqrt(n) l_i; the repair is two displayed lines, needs no new lemma, construction, or reoptimization, and no theorem, algorithm, rate, guarantee, or experimental conclusion is lost. By the severity rubric this is a short, local, routine repair preserving every substantive claim.
